### LOW: Erasure threat model omits the new irreversible Privy user deletion and the outbox's retention of the Privy DID
[coordinator/internal/store/erasure/keys\.go:147](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/d5172dacdf8c9374150ef64098c3ab494b06a47d/coordinator/internal/store/erasure/keys.go#L147) · T-059

This PR adds a privy\_user outbox target\. OutboxRows\(\) \(keys\.go:147\-149\) stores the raw Privy DID as ExternalID, even though the users rule overwrites users\.privy\_user\_id with 'erased:<uuid>'\. The DID therefore persists in erasure\_outbox until the worker finishes\. PrivyAuth\.DeleteUser \(privy\_delete\_user\.go:21\-52\) then makes an irreversible, app\-secret\-authenticated call to auth\.privy\.io\. The T\-059 threat model and its mitigations do not cover this\. Two cases need a fix or an explicit mitigation entry: \(a\) an outbox row delivered before the grace period ends, followed by Cancel, would leave a restored account whose Privy identity is gone and could lock the user out\. \(b\) a wrong or stale DID would delete another person's Privy identity\. Fix: add privy\_user to T\-059 and record in affected\_files that Privy deletion is delivered only after the scrub commits\. Require the worker to confirm ownership of the DID, and clear external\_id once the row is delivered\. Add coordinator/auth/privy\_delete\_user\.go and outbox\.go to T\-059's affected files\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Cancelling an erasure re\-enables any credential whose DeletedAt matches the confirm stamp, including ones revoked during the grace period
[coordinator/store/memory/erasure\.go:213](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/d5172dacdf8c9374150ef64098c3ab494b06a47d/coordinator/store/memory/erasure.go#L213) · A-007, A-008, T-059

CancelAccountErasure now un\-revokes API keys and provider tokens \(head lines 213\-221\)\. Previously they stayed revoked\. A credential counts as 'removed by confirm' only if DeletedAt equals RequestedAt \(or the AlreadyRevoked stamp\)\. A key or token that an admin or the incident process disabled or deactivated after the confirm, for example because it was found compromised, normally keeps the confirm's DeletedAt\. Cancelling then sets Disabled to false and Active to true, so a deliberately revoked credential becomes usable again\. The same applies to providers \(line 209\)\. The restore logic cannot tell 'revoked by the confirm' from 'revoked later'\. T\-059 and its mitigation text still say the confirm revokes credentials\. The credential\-restoration semantics on cancel are not described in the threat model\. Fix: record which credential IDs the confirm revoked, or stamp later revocations with a distinct sentinel\. Restore only that set, and document the cancel semantics in T\-059\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5
